description: Floating bottom navigation covers lower list rows and cards because screens lack matching bottom scroll clearance.
example_quotes: Floating tab bar overlaps the first training-log row. The log's content continues behind it and is hard to scan or tap.
Training-log rows appear under the floating navigation bar. Add actual scroll content inset or relocate navigation.

description: Selected French language does not propagate to all counts, stage names, date labels and fixture-derived content.
example_quotes: French live round still labels the stage ROUND 1. Use the selected app language consistently in the camera UI.
French recap still says rounds and drill. Decide whether these are intentional boxing loanwords; current mixed register differs from the rest of the French UI.

description: Large title cards consume the first viewport and push the workout or review action/evidence below it.
example_quotes: Two-line display title consumes about a quarter of the first screen. The camera start and chosen session sit below a long introduction, making entry feel like reading a poster rather than entering a workout.
The English headline takes nearly the full width and dominates the initial viewport. Reduce its type size and vertical block to bring the start action higher.

description: Live bottom overlay uses a larger timer/button stack than needed for glanceable coaching over camera footage.
example_quotes: The bottom HUD is tall and the red Start button fills most of its width. The camera area is visually clear in simulator, but usable framing with a real image is unverified.
The timer and Pause control dominate the bottom of the camera view. Make the timer and controls compact enough to read at a glance without masking feet or bag action.

description: Light text on the warm ivory film notebook destroys hierarchy and legibility in both languages.
example_quotes: White title, subtitle, section labels and status-bar text sit on warm ivory; several are nearly invisible. Correct color tokens before any further styling.
The same white-on-ivory failure hides the French film title and section labels. This persists across both languages.

description: Session log and calendar use bulky system grouped-list proportions instead of the established compact noir language.
example_quotes: Dense grouped Form card, large navigation header and repeated planned rows abandon the compact editorial style of the entry and live views. Collapse untouched future rounds and elevate observed segments.
A single tall system-style card dominates the planning screen, with large blank space beneath the month grid. Distinguish calendar dates from log rows and keep the card proportional to the content.

description: Too many competing entry elements weaken the one-tap camera start.
example_quotes: Duration row, oversized red CTA and explanatory floor-angle paragraph form three stacked calls for attention. Preserve the corner mark, but reduce secondary copy and make the start control the single focus.
Large duration boxes and saturated button compete with the large title. Establish one accent use and a smaller control scale.

description: Fixed three-column metric layout does not fit longer French labels and causes actual overlap.
example_quotes: French stat labels overlap: ÉCHANTILLONS CAMÉRA runs into CONSIGNES DEMANDÉES. Three equal columns do not accommodate the French strings.

description: A technically precise completed-round count appears contradictory beside a reached-round card.
example_quotes: 0 timed rounds appears above a Round 1 reached card. Both are technically distinguishable, but the hierarchy makes the report look self-contradictory. Lead with time trained and rounds reached, then label completed full rounds separately.

description: Technical server controls and telemetry explanations intrude into the consumer film flow.
example_quotes: Connection settings foreground URL, access key and pose telemetry in a large technical sheet reached from the film notebook. Keep this out of the first-use coaching journey and use compact support copy.
